subject: VoltaSense reserved-capacity cushion & SKU allocation question
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@voltasense.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VoltaSense reserved-capacity cushion & SKU allocation question

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. We pulled together a first-pass proposal (attached) but had two quick asks before we send a redline-ready contract:

1) Cushioning approach: Your forecast shows a sharp ramp in Nov–Dec. To protect both sides from GPU price volatility, would VoltaSense consider a 10% buffer on top of committed vGPU-hours for the initial 6 months (to be billed only if used)? We can structure it as an optional committed cushion with a fixed blended discount.

2) SKU mix: Our ops team prefers a 70/20/10 split (A100-like / A40-like / burst T4-class) to balance latency vs cost. The attached "proposed_sku_mix_v1.pdf" includes a few alternative mixes if you want to prioritize cost over tail latency.

If you can confirm tolerance on the cushion and which SKU mix you prefer, we’ll produce a final term-sheet with the pricing-breakpoints and approval path for the discount.

Quick ask: are you okay if I loop in Finance (David) for a one-time approval step on the pass-through guardrail?

Cheers,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: VoltaSense_usage_forecast_Q3-Q4_2025.xlsx (xlsx), proposed_sku_mix_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Moreno <alex@voltasense.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VoltaSense reserved-capacity cushion & SKU allocation question

Hannah —

Appreciate the follow-up and the draft. Quick answers:

1) Cushioning: We can accept an optional 10% cushion for Q3–Q4 as you suggested, provided it's capped per quarter and the blended discount on cushion usage is no deeper than the committed rate minus 5%. We need visibility into the exact billing trigger (daily callout vs monthly reconciliation).

2) SKU mix: We like the 70/20/10 split as a starting point. If costs spike >15% vs today's baseline, we need an automatic fallback to increase the T4-class burst pool and throttle the high-cost SKUs to preserve spend predictability.

Yes — loop Finance in. Please include an example invoice reconciliation line so our CFO can see how cushion consumption is surfaced.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Engineering, VoltaSense
alex@voltasense.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VoltaSense reserved-capacity cushion & SKU allocation question

Thanks Alex — solid inputs.

David — quick context: VoltaSense is willing to take a 10% optional cushion capped per quarter and expects an auto-fallback trigger if GPU costs rise >15%. They want the cushion billed only on consumption and want the invoice to show cushion lines separately.

David, can you confirm whether Finance will accept a blended cushion rate that is the committed rate minus up to 5%? If not, what floor do we need to present to the customer to get approval? Also, what internal approval path is needed if we offer a conditional SKU fallback clause (i.e., automatic throttle to T4-class at specified cost thresholds)?

I put the forecast in Drive: https://drive.google.com/voltasense/forecast_Q3Q4

-Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VoltaSense reserved-capacity cushion & SKU allocation question

Marissa / Hannah —

Thanks for the tag. High level: Finance is okay with an optional cushion billed on consumption, with the following constraints:

- Cushion discount floor: committed rate minus 3% (i.e., max 3% cheaper than committed unit price)
- Quarterly cap: cushion consumption cannot exceed 12% of the committed vGPU-hours for that quarter without executive approval
- Reporting: cushion consumption must be presented as a distinct line item on the invoice; we need daily aggregated utilization metrics (CSV) and monthly reconciliation.

On the automatic fallback (throttle to T4-class) if GPU costs spike >15%: Finance will approve productizing the clause only if we include a clear customer notification window (72 hours) and a one-time mitigation credit of up to $25k if the throttle materially impacts production SLAs in the first month after activation.

Internal approvals required: VP Finance sign-off (I will route), and pricing exception from Revenue Ops if the expected margin impact exceeds 6% for year-1. Please supply modeled margin scenarios (baseline, +10% cost shock, +25% cost shock) showing revenue, gross margin, and expected NRR impact. Marissa / Hannah — can you get those numbers to me by EOD Friday?

-David
David Kim
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@voltasense.ai>, CFO, VoltaSense <cfo@voltasense.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: VoltaSense reserved-capacity cushion & SKU allocation question

Alex / VoltaSense team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and alignment. Per Finance guidance below (copied):

- We can offer the optional 10% per-quarter cushion billed on consumption at committed rate minus up to 3%.
- Cushion consumption above 12% quarterly cap requires exec approval.
- If GPU costs spike >15% we will automatically shift traffic to the agreed T4-class burst pool after a 72-hour notification window; Redwood will provide a one-time mitigation credit up to $25k if production SLAs are materially affected in the first 30 days post-activation.

Next steps:
- Marissa: I asked for three margin scenarios and will share the final term-sheet once David signs off.
- Alex / CFO: if these guardrails are acceptable, say so and we’ll send a DocuSign with the cushion appendix and SKU table.

Thanks — Hannah
